::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** September 28th 1874  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Pierpont Morgan Library, New York, MA 2768
:::

My dear [Florence](people/person_1520.qmd)

Publishing on commission does mean taking the risk and paying a percentage, above the expenses to the publisher.  It is what I often do, always with [Mozley](organizations/other_108.qmd)  The round sum for each edition is pleasant, and I don’t think you would get so much in the end by this as by selling copy right.  But if Mr Cowie[^1] has answered you and is considering is there much use in my writing to him.  I would do it if it were to ensure his attention, but I think he will give that, and if one writes without necessity, it is rather wasting one’s recommending power and making it less effective when it is really needed  I wish [Ward](organizations/other_235.qmd) would take the story, but he declined Chardham Fair,[^2] which I thought would have made beautiful illustrations and he has taken such stupid stories instead that I cannot judge of him

your affectionate

C M Yonge

&nbsp;

---

[^1]: ‘Mozley, Cowie and Smith’ appears briefly in 1874 as the imprint of the firm that was formerly [John & Charles Mozley](organizations/other_108.qmd) (1845-1874) and became Mozley & Smith in 1875. Mr Cowie may have been the “foreman they took into partnership [who] immediately went mad, and upset the arrangements - and they had to go on paying him as partner after he was in an asylum, till the firm could be dissolved.” [CMY to Bartholomew Price 1882]
[^2]: Evelyn Tod, Chardham Fair, an historical tale serialised in MP from January - September1873.
